flash: Choose whether to put your %{DEVICE_NAME} into Force Recovery Mode via Manual Setup or Automatic Setup. Choose Automatic Setup only if the device has already been flashed and is currently running.
recoveryAuto: Ensure the device has already been flashed, powered and running.
Connect the host computer to the back USB Type-C connector on the device.
Connect your device to a monitor with the SOC's DP out (one below the HDHM-IN).
Enter the connection information of your %{DEVICE_NAME}.
recoveryManual: Make sure the device is connected to the power adapter, and the ATX switch above the cable is powered on.
Connect the host computer to the USB Type-C connector on the device.
Connect the host computer to the device with an ethernet cable.

Set your host ethernet adapter ip to "192.168.1.100"
- Assuming your ethernet adapter is "eth0", you can:
 - a. Run "nmcli dev disconnect eth0" on your host to make sure the port is dicconnected.
 - b. Run "sudo ip addr add 192.168.1.100/24 dev eth0" on your host to set up ip.

SSH to your target device BMC with "ssh root@192.168.1.110"
- The default password is "0penBmc", and you will need to change your password on first time attempt.

With your SSH connection to the device BMC
- a. Run "powerctrl power_on" to turn on the device's CPU.(This is equivalent to pressing the button on the front of your device.)
- b. Run "powerctrl recovery" to put the device into recovery mode.
Connect your device to a monitor with the SOC's DP out (one below the HDHM-IN).
targetAccess: Complete the Ubuntu 'System configuration wizard' on your %{targetName}, if you have chosen to configure it manually before flashing.
Wait for the OS login screen.
If proxy is used on host, also configure apt proxy on your %{targetName}.
Enter the username and password of your %{targetName}.
